name: Gaudi HPU Graphs: Static Shape Capture and Replay
workarounds: Use torch.compile with mode='reduce-overhead' to enable HPU graphs
Use static shapes (fixed batch size and sequence length) to avoid graph recompilation
Use the vLLM Gaudi plugin's custom graph caching for fast warm-up
notes: HPU graphs are Gaudi's equivalent of CUDA graphs: they capture a sequence of kernel launches into a single graph that can be replayed with minimal launch overhead. This is critical for LLM inference where many small kernel launches (attention, FFN, sampling) would otherwise be launch-bound. The vLLM Gaudi plugin implements custom graph caching for fast warm-up and efficient memory use. torch.compile with mode='reduce-overhead' enables HPU graphs automatically. The key constraint is static shapes: the batch size and sequence length must be fixed at capture time, so any change triggers recompilation. This is why vLLM on Gaudi uses a bucketing mechanism to group requests into fixed-size buckets. The HabanaAI/vllm-fork reached EOL at v1.23.0; the vllm-gaudi plugin is the production path. HPU graphs are not portable to CUDA or ROCm; they are a Gaudi-specific feature that requires the Habana runtime (torch-hpu).
